findings.message: The round-17 fix is only partly a class fix. The `for update` lock is in the shared `assignProposals`, so the code covers both callers. The new cross-release race table only drives `createRelease(v2, [p])`, though. The previous finding also named the same cross-release race for `setReleaseProposals` on a different, already existing release, and that case still has no test in either order. `setReleaseProposals` locks its own release (v2) before calling `assignProposals`. Any read or check it makes before that call is not covered. If a later change moves its phase or release check ahead of the row lock, no test fails. Fix: add `setReleaseProposals(v2, [p])` rows to this `it.each` table, with v2 created empty beforehand. Cover move-first (hold on the `for update` select) and deploy-first (hold on the released update). Assert the same end states: proposed under v2, or released under v1 with 'already shipped in another release'.
findings.scenario: p in v1, empty release v2 exists. In session A, recordDeployment(v1, Prod) is held after `update delivery.proposal set phase = 'released'`. Session B then calls setReleaseProposals(v2, [p]). No test checks that B waits and is refused. A regression that reads p's phase before the lock would set release_id = v2 on a released row, and every test would still pass.

findings.message: The new row lock is taken one row at a time, in the caller's key order. A Prod deployment's `update delivery.proposal set phase = 'released' where release_id = …` locks the same rows in scan order, and two createRelease/setReleaseProposals calls lock them in whatever order their key lists give. With two or more shared proposals, the lock orders can cross. Postgres then aborts one transaction with a raw 40P01 'deadlock detected' error instead of a clear refusal or a serialised result. The new tests use a single proposal, so they cannot show this. Fix: lock every target row in one deterministic statement (`select … where key = any(${keys}) and project_id = … order by id for update`). Lock v1's proposal rows the same way (order by id) before the deploy's update. Then add a two-proposal race test.
findings.scenario: v1 holds [p, q]. createRelease(v2, [q, p]) runs at the same time as recordDeployment(v1, Prod). The move locks q and then waits on p, while the deploy's update has locked p and waits on q. One of them fails with 'deadlock detected'.
